sol.section: Recommended exact spec diff: §8.3 opening requirement, exact-entry exception and legacy handling

steps.claim: Epsilon expressions use exact rational arithmetic. An eps-independent expression evaluating to zero is an exact native match for §17 item 9, and §4.4 requires the exact phase-fixed operation at epsilon zero.
The diff requires a realisation_model for every expression-valued epsilon, but subsequently permits exact entries to omit it and denote the exact opcode.

Take conformance/fixtures/controlled-action-09/target.json and replace gates[0].epsilon with {"op":"-","args":[1,1]}, leaving realisation_model absent. The epsilon is exactly zero and independent of eps, while its syntax is expression-valued.

The opening rule requires a model for this entry; the exact-entry exception permits omission. Consequently the diff does not consistently determine whether the exact controlled-X obligation is checkable or missing-model unchecked.

sol.fix: In §8.3, replace the opening requirement and reconcile the exact-entry and migration sentences as follows: “A native entry MUST supply a versioned realisation_model if its epsilon can evaluate to a nonzero value in an admitted resolved context. An entry whose epsilon is independent of eps and evaluates to zero in every admitted context MAY omit the model and then denotes the exact §4.4 opcode, including global phase and controlled form. A supplied model MUST agree with that exact operation in every zero-epsilon context and satisfy the advertised bound otherwise. For legacy entries lacking a required model, missing-model unchecked reporting applies only to nonzero-epsilon contexts.” The 1−1 fixture must remain exact and checkable without a model. For a legacy X entry with epsilon={"var":"c"} covering c=0..1, c=0 denotes exact X without a model; c=1 remains missing-model unchecked. Alternatively, require models for every expression syntax and explicitly restrict the omission exception to literal zero, documenting that validation change. Prefer the value-based repair, which preserves the existing exact-entry convention.

codex.section: Recommended exact spec diff, §8.3 model requirement and exact-entry exemption

steps.claim: Existing exact-native matching includes epsilon expressions independent of eps that evaluate to zero.
The proposed opening requires a model for every expression-valued epsilon, while its closing rule permits exact entries to omit the model.
An X entry with epsilon {"op":"-","args":[1,1]} and no model evaluates exactly to zero. It qualifies for the exact exemption but violates the opening MUST.
steps.by: clause:§8.1 expression evaluation; witness:exact rational evaluation 1−1=0

steps.claim: One checker can use the exact X matrix while another reports a missing-model obligation for the same entry. The amendment gives incompatible verification requirements.

codex.fix: In §8.3 replace the opening requirement and align the exact-entry paragraph: “Model requirements are determined by evaluated epsilon, not expression syntax. At each resolved invocation context with epsilon zero, an omitted model denotes exactly the §4.4 opcode, including global phase and controlled form. A positive evaluated epsilon requires a realisation model to discharge independent realised-operation verification; a legacy entry lacking it leaves that obligation unchecked. Any supplied model MUST satisfy the exact contract at zero epsilon and the advertised bound at positive epsilon.” Expected result: epsilon {"op":"-","args":[1,1]} without a model is treated as exact X, with no missing-model diagnostic.

codex.section: Recommended exact spec diff, §8.3 kind/channel admission; interactions with §§4.4 and 12.3
codex.problem: The diff admits kind=channel with CPTP normalization but leaves epsilon as the existing accuracy obligation. §4.4 defines that obligation for a realised unitary in operator norm; a general channel has no such unitary. §12.3 additionally requires a numerical claim for a controlled unitary variant. For example, the proposed expression language admits Kraus operators K0=X/√2 and K1=ZX/√2. They satisfy ΣK†K=I, but map |+><+| to I/2, so no logical unitary represents them. Supplying a controlled dilation does not make the reduced logical channel unitary. The amendment never decides whether this valid channel model is inadmissible as a native gate or is admitted under a new diamond-error contract. This is a semantic admission and certificate-verdict decision, not a missing encoding detail.
codex.fix: For this K repair I recommend retaining §4.4’s native-unitary contract. In §8.3 state: “Every native model MUST identify a phase-bearing logical unitary U for each resolved parameter/control context. A Kraus or instrument representation is admissible as a native gate model only when its reduced logical map equals ρ↦UρU†, and U, including phase relative to disabled control branches, is also bound. Native epsilon bounds ||U−V||op against §4.4’s corresponding ideal V. Channel claims may compare the induced channels but do not replace §12.3’s required numerical claims for controlled unitary variants.” The two-Kraus dephasing example must fail native-unitary conformance; X and −X unitary models remain available with the stated error obligations. Alternatively, retain genuinely nonunitary native models and amend §§4.4, 8.1 and 12.3 explicitly: “For channel models, epsilon is a diamond-norm bound against the ideal opcode channel in the specified control context; it is charged as diamond without ×2 conversion, requires channel claims, and cannot establish an operator-norm or exact-inverse conclusion.” That alternative also needs an explicit exception to the existing native-unitary admission rule.
